עכשיו ב-Google Play: שימוש הרבה פחות בזיכרון, וצליל פתיחה

items.title: חדש ב-1.09: כמה גלים יחד
items.ticker: חדש ב-1.09: כמה גלים יחד ותופים בזמן אמת
items.summary: ב-Google Play, גרסה 1.09: על כל כפתור גל יש אייקון של הגל. לחיצה ארוכה מוסיפה או מורידה גל, כך שקליד אחד מנגן כמה גלים יחד, והפריסטים זוכרים אילו גלים דולקים. לחיצה ארוכה על Presets שומרת את הפריסט הטעון, והחלון נפתח בעמוד שלו. במסך התופים, BPM, Swing והווליום של השורות שמשנים תוך כדי נגינה עוברים לפטרנים הבאים.
imageAlts: מסך Sound בגרסה 1.09: אייקון על כל כפתור גל, Sine ו-Saw דולקים יחד.

items.title: Sound FX + צבעים לעמודי הלופר
items.ticker: Sound FX וצבעים לעמודי הלופר
items.summary: מאז גרסה 1.08: 8 אפקטי Sound FX חדשים שהולכים לפי הביט של התופים, ואפשר להחליף ביניהם תוך כדי נגינה. פריסטים שומרים את ההגדרות של כל ה-8. לכל עמוד בלופר יש שם ואחד מ-8 צבעים. הנובים מראים את הערך בטבעת זהב, והמדריך באפליקציה מלמד את כל זה.
imageAlts: חלון Sound FX עם Psy Orbit נבחר.
מסך Loop עם מספרי עמודים צבעוניים ושם עמוד.

items.title: חבילות Exclusive ב-Pro
items.ticker: Exclusive ב-Pro
items.summary: מאז גרסה 1.08: מי שקונה Pro מקבל גם את חבילת Exclusive בחינם, בלי עלות נוספת. אלה 11 ערכות תופים Exclusive באפליקציה, בנוסף ל-Factory 64. אין כפתור הורדה. האתר רק מציג מידע על הערכות.
imageAlts: פוסטר Exclusive ל-Pro: 11 ערכות תופים, פתיחה מתוך האפליקציה.

items.title: מצב Live, מילים, Mic FX ו-Drum FX
items.ticker: מצב Live, מילים, Mic FX ו-Drum FX
items.summary: מאז גרסה 1.08: מצב LIVE נועל שמות, Clear וטעינת קבצים בזמן נגינה. חלון המילים גולל את הטקסט בזמן שאתם שרים. למיקרופון ולתופים יש 8 אפקטים לכל אחד, לכל ערוץ לופ יש Looper FX, וכפתור Back אחד מחזיר את ההקלטה האחרונה שנמחקה.
imageAlts: חלון המילים פתוח מעל האפליקציה.
לוח Mic FX. Phone Line נבחר.

launch.headline: זמין עכשיו ב-Google Play.
launch.note: זמין עכשיו ב-Google Play. L Studio Pro, ‏24.90 ‏₪.

sound-presets.title: Presets: 8 מקומות, 8 עמודים
sound-presets.text: פריסט שומר את הסאונד יחד עם Sound FX והגלים הדולקים. לחיצה ארוכה על Presets שומרת לפריסט שטעון.

sound-scales.title: Key וסקאלות
sound-scales.text: בוחרים Major או Minor מכל תו שורש, מ-C עד B. סולם רק מסמן את הקלידים שלו ולא משנה את התדרים שלהם.

mic-channels.title: ערוצים עם סאונד משלהם
mic-channels.text: שישה ערוצים בשני עמודים. לכל ערוץ HPF, Pres, FX, עוצמה ו-L/R משלו, ועוד השתקה וסולו.

mic-fx.title: Mic FX לכל ערוץ
mic-fx.text: שמונה פריסטים. הקשה בוחרת, הקשה נוספת מכבה, ולחיצה ארוכה פותחת את המחוונים, כולל Transpose מ-‎-12 עד 12.

loop-looper.title: 32 ערוצים, 8 עמודים
loop-looper.text: ארבעה ערוצים בכל עמוד. הקלטה יכולה להימשך עד 30 דקות, ו-Redo מחזיר הקלטה שמחקתם.

loop-editor.title: Loop Editor
loop-editor.text: חותכים את ההקלטה, קובעים את נקודות הלופ ומעצבים עם EQ, Gain ו-Squeeze. שמונה תיבות קושרות את הלופ לקצב תופים.

loop-fx.title: Looper FX
loop-fx.text: שמונה פריסטים לערוץ. הקשה בוחרת, ולחיצה ארוכה פותחת Amount, EQ, Mid-sweep, Transpose ו-Reverb שלו.

loop-page-name.title: שם וצבע לעמוד
loop-page-name.text: לחיצה ארוכה על מספר עמוד פותחת את Page name. מקלידים שם ובוחרים אחד מ-8 צבעים. הצבע גם צובע את הגלים של העמוד.

sound-fx.title: Sound FX
sound-fx.text: שמונה אפקטים שעוקבים אחרי קצב התופים, אחד פעיל בכל רגע. לחיצה ארוכה פותחת את המחוונים: Amount, EQ, Mid-sweep, Transpose ו-Reverb.

sound-keyboards.title: שתי מקלדות
sound-keyboards.text: לוחצים על + לפתיחת מקלדת שנייה, אוקטבה אחת גבוה יותר. היא נשארת פתוחה במעבר בין Sound ל-Pad.

mic-editor.title: Mic Editor
mic-editor.text: הקשה על הוויזואלייזר של ערוץ פותחת אותו כשיש בערוץ הקלטה. חיתוך, לולאה, EQ, Gain ו-Squeeze, עם 8 תיבות קצב. Save שומר את השינויים בפרויקט המיקרופון.

mic-lyrics.title: טלפרומפטר למילים
mic-lyrics.text: הקשה על Edit מאפשרת להקליד או להדביק מילים. Play גולל אותן ו-Pause עוצר. Speed נע בין 20 ל-150 וגודל הטקסט בין 14 ל-48. הכול נשמר בפלאפון.

pad-live.title: משטח חי
pad-live.text: מחזיקים צליל וגוררים על המשטח. הצליל עוקב אחרי האצבע כל עוד הצליל מנגן. WAH, OCT ו-Vibrato הם נובים מ-0 עד 100 אחוז שמעצבים רק את צליל המקלדת.

pad-keyboard.title: מקלדת שנייה ב-Pad
pad-keyboard.text: לוחצים על + ליד שורת VOICES לפתיחת מקלדת שנייה, אוקטבה אחת גבוה יותר. הנובים WAH, OCT ו-Vibrato מוסתרים כשהיא פתוחה.

pad-targets.title: יעדי המשטח
pad-targets.text: KEY, MIC, LOOP ו-DRUM קובעים מה המשטח מזיז, ואפשר להדליק כמה יחד. מחזיקים 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 או 1/32 כדי לחזור עליהם במהירות בקצב ה-BPM של התופים, ומחזיקים STOP כדי להחליש אותם בהדרגה.

drum-rows.title: כל 8 השורות
drum-rows.text: הקשה על +4 מציגה את FX 1, FX 2, FX 3 ו-Voice מתחת לארבע השורות הראשונות ומסתירה את המקלדת. המקש מתחלף ל-‎-4, והקשה נוספת מסתירה את השורות ומחזירה את המקלדת.

drum-main.title: מסך Drum
drum-main.text: החצים מחליפים קיט וסאמפלים, והנובים קובעים Drum Vol, Swing ו-BPM. לכל אחד מ-8 המקצבים יש 16 צעדים בכל שורה. בכל שורה יש LOAD, חצים, סליידר ווליום ו-L/R. הקשה על +4 מציגה את FX 1, FX 2, FX 3 ו-Voice.

drum-banks.title: בנקי סאמפלים
drum-banks.text: שמונה שורות, והקשה על שם שורה פותחת את רשימת הסאונדים שלה מהבנקים Factory ו-Exclusive. כל שורה מציגה רק סוג סאונד משלה.

drum-loaded.title: הסאמפלים שלכם (LOADED)
drum-loaded.text: בכל אחת מ-8 השורות יש בנק LOADED של עד 88 סאמפלים משלכם, עד 30 שניות כל אחד, שנשמר לבד. פסי ההתחלה והסוף חותכים את הסאמפל. SAVE שומר, RESET מחזיר לאורך מלא, RENAME נותן שם של עד 24 תווים ו-DELETE מוחק.

drum-fx.title: Drum FX
drum-fx.text: שמונה פריסטים לתופים. הקשה מדליקה, הקשה נוספת מכבה, ולחיצה ארוכה פותחת את המחוונים.

drum-repeats.title: Pattern repeats
drum-repeats.text: לחיצה ארוכה על מספר קצב פותחת את החלון. בוחרים 1 עד 10, מקלידים מספר עד 88 בתיבה, או בוחרים אינסוף או DEFAULT. COPY ו-PASTE מעבירים קצב שלם למספר אחר.

home-sound.title: עצבו את הצליל שלכם
home-sound.text: שלבו סוגי גל, התחילו מצליל מוכן וכוונו כל קליד לסולם שלכם.
home-sound.alt: 1/8: עצבו את הצליל שלכם. שלבו סוגי גל, התחילו מצליל מוכן וכוונו כל קליד לסולם שלכם.

home-sound-fx.title: צבעו כל צליל
home-sound-fx.text: בחרו עולם אפקטים לקלידים ולתופים, וכווננו את הגוון שלו.
home-sound-fx.alt: 2/8: צבעו כל צליל. בחרו עולם אפקטים לקלידים ולתופים, וכווננו את הגוון שלו.

home-looper.title: בנו שכבות של לולאות
home-looper.text: הקליטו לולאות ערוץ אחר ערוץ, חתכו אותן לפי הקצב ובנו מהן קטע שלם.
home-looper.alt: 3/8: בנו שכבות של לולאות. הקליטו לולאות ערוץ אחר ערוץ, חתכו אותן לפי הקצב ובנו מהן קטע שלם.

home-live-pad.title: נגנו בזמן אמת
home-live-pad.text: שנו את הצליל באצבע אחת והפעילו חזרות בקצב תוך כדי הופעה.
home-live-pad.alt: 4/8: נגנו בזמן אמת. שנו את הצליל באצבע אחת והפעילו חזרות בקצב תוך כדי הופעה.

home-drums.title: בנו את הקצב שלכם
home-drums.text: תכנתו תבניות צעד אחר צעד, בחרו כל תוף מתוך ספריות דגימות ועצבו אותו.
home-drums.alt: 5/8: בנו את הקצב שלכם. תכנתו תבניות צעד אחר צעד, בחרו כל תוף מתוך ספריות דגימות ועצבו אותו.

home-mixer.title: המיקסר האנלוגי שלכם
home-mixer.text: ראו היכן יושבים התופים, הלולאות והמיקרופון, ועצבו מהם מיקס אחד מאוזן.
home-mixer.alt: 6/8: המיקסר האנלוגי שלכם. ראו היכן יושבים התופים, הלולאות והמיקרופון, ועצבו מהם מיקס אחד מאוזן.

home-mastering-style.title: סיימו את השיר
home-mastering-style.text: בחרו סגנון צליל, השוו לפני ואחרי וייצאו את הקובץ הסופי.
home-mastering-style.alt: 7/8: סיימו את השיר. בחרו סגנון צליל, השוו לפני ואחרי וייצאו את הקובץ הסופי.

home-mastering-measure.title: מדדו כל פרט
home-mastering-measure.text: מדידה מדויקת של עוצמה, דינמיקה וסטריאו מראה איך השיר שלכם נשמע באמת.
home-mastering-measure.alt: 8/8: מדדו כל פרט. מדידה מדויקת של עוצמה, דינמיקה וסטריאו מראה איך השיר שלכם נשמע באמת.

sound-wave-panel.title: לוח הגל: אוקטבה, גוון ודפים
sound-wave-panel.text: לחיצה ארוכה על מקש גל פותחת את הלוח שלו: מקשי האוקטבה -2, -1, 0, +1 ו-+2, הכפתורים LOW, MID, HIGH, HPF, LPF ו-GAIN, ו-4 דפים, כל דף עוד קול של אותו גל. כל שינוי נשמע מיד ונשמר.

loop-mixer.title: מיקסר אנלוגי
loop-mixer.text: הקשה על LIVE SCOPE פותחת אותו. לתופים, ללופר ולמיק יש Drive, HPF, EQ, Comp, Pan, Width ופיידר, ועוד ערוץ Master. SPECTRUM ו-MIX MAP מראים איפה הם מתנגשים. 8 פריסטים.

mic-mastering.title: מאסטרינג
mic-mastering.text: אחרי הקלטת WAV פותחים אותו ב-Master this take. בוחרים אחד מ-8 סגנונות, משווים בין A ל-B, ומייצאים ל-WAV, MP3 או FLAC. הקבצים נשארים בפלאפון.

hero.kicker: Android music app · Version 1.12, on Google Play now
hero.title: Make music on your phone.
hero.body: L Studio is a music-making app for your Android phone. Record loops, add drums, sing with the lyrics in front of you, and if you want to go beyond the usual notes, tune every key to its own frequency.

meet.title: Meet L-studio
meet.body: Open the short and meet the app.

signalStrip.text: From key ← to sound ← to loop ← to recording

story.title: It all started with a note that wasn't there.
body: There's do, re, mi, fa, sol, la and si.
One day I asked myself, why only seven?
Suddenly another sound popped into my head. "Al."
That's where the first idea for L-Studio was born. I wanted to build a keyboard where I could set which frequency belongs to each key myself.
I never planned to build a big app. I wanted an instrument.
Then I wanted to record what I played, so I built a WAV recorder. Then I wanted a looper. Then drums. Then a microphone.
And every time I asked myself, why not add that too?
That's how, little by little, the instrument became a whole app for making music.
story.closing: What started as a search for the eighth note became L-Studio.

featuresIntro.title: Just open it and play.
featuresIntro.body: You don't need to know music to start. Open it, touch it, change it, listen, and see what happens.

underHood.title: There's a lot going on behind the scenes.
underHood.body: L-Studio was built to give you control over sound without forcing you to learn a giant system. The keys, the sound, the effects, the microphone, the looper, the pad and the drums all work inside the same app. You can also manually tune the frequency of every key and build your keyboard your way.
underHood.closing: The complexity lives in the engine. Not in the way you have to use it.

details.label: MANUAL TUNING
details.value: Set an exact frequency for every key and build your own scale

details.label: VOICE LAYER
details.value: Wave, Octave, Glide, ADSR, Cutoff and Resonance

details.label: PERFORMANCE FLOW
details.value: Keys, microphone, looper, pad and drums work inside the same flow

details.label: EFFECTS + MIX
details.value: Echo, effects, and an Analog Mixer with Drive, EQ, Comp, Pan and a Master strip

details.label: CAPTURE
details.value: Local recording, WAV export, and Mastering to WAV, MP3 and FLAC

underHood.specsBody: A practical view of what happens between touch and sound.

justStart.title: There's a lot to do. You don't need to know it all.
body: When you open music software for the first time, the first thing you might feel is that there's too much going on.
Buttons, windows, menus, and all kinds of things you don't know what they do.
L-Studio was built differently. There's a lot here, but you can start without taking a course.
Open a button. Touch it. Listen.
After a few minutes you already start understanding what everything does.
justStart.closing: Start playing. The rest will come.

factoryPack.lede: The sound is already waiting for you.
factoryPack.shortText: 8 preset pages. 8 drum kits. Ready to play.
factoryPack.description: L Studio Pro comes with the full Factory Pack: 8 synth preset pages (64 voices), then 8 drum kits with 8 styles in each kit (64 styles in all, not 64 kits). Pick a sound or a kit, load it, and start playing.
factoryPack.coverAlt: L Studio Pro pack covers side by side: Factory 64 with 64 presets on 8 pages, Drum Kits with 8 kits and 8 styles, and Exclusive with 11 drum packs

vision.title: I built the app I needed.
vision.author: David Chatam, L-Studio developer
body: I don't come from a background of music studies. I never learned how to build professional music software, and I didn't have a big system to work with.
I just love music and wanted to control sound in a way that felt natural to me.
It all started from the idea of setting the frequencies of the keys myself. From there I added recording, a looper, drums, a microphone and other things I needed along the way.
I want to build a community around L Studio of people who love music. Even if you don't have a computer or expensive software, you can create with the phone you already have.
vision.mainLine: It's for analog people in a digital world.

cards.title: Just start
cards.body: Open the app and start creating without feeling like you need to know everything first.

cards.title: Play with sound
cards.body: Touch the sound, change it, and discover things you didn't plan.

cards.title: Take your music with you
cards.body: Creating shouldn't have to wait for a computer. If you have an idea, you can start from it right now.

items.question: Is L Studio on Google Play yet, and how much is it?
answer: L Studio Pro for Android is available now on Google Play, for $8, with version 1.12, which brings the Analog Mixer and the Mastering window. It is a one-time payment. New versions arrive as automatic updates through Google Play once they are approved. Version 1.13 is in Google review and is not available yet.
Once it is released, you buy it through Google Play. This website does not sell the app and has no download button.

items.question: What does Pro include? Is there a free version?
answer: There is a single version of the app: Pro. It is the whole app: the Factory Pack with 64 presets and eight drum kits, and also the eleven Exclusive drum packs, at no extra cost. There is no download button for Exclusive.
Pro has no ads, and everything in it is open from the first launch.
A free demo is coming soon, and it will be downloadable from this website.
You can see the Exclusive packs on the Exclusive page of this site.

items.question: Which devices does it run on, and in which languages?
answer: L Studio is an Android app. It needs Android 7.0 or newer. Version 1.12 is 78.3 MB. There is no iPhone version for now.
It was tested on various Android phones. It was not tested on tablets, so tablet support is not promised.
On a phone the app stays upright, in portrait.
The app comes in four languages: English, Hebrew, Russian, and Arabic. You switch in Settings, on the Language row.

items.question: Does it work offline? Does anyone see my music?
answer: Yes, it works without an internet connection. The app does not ask for internet access at all.
The only permission it asks for is the microphone, the first time you tap Rec. You can take it back at any time in your phone's settings.
Your recordings, presets, and sessions stay on your phone, or wherever you choose to save them. The app has no ads and no analytics.

items.question: I'm new to this. Where do I start?
answer: Open the app and touch things. You don't need a course.
In Settings, Show tutorial starts a short tour. The tour has a menu of stations: you can skip, resume where you left off, or finish from the menu.
The user guide on this site has nine topics, including the Analog Mixer and Mastering. Each one ends with three tips for beginners and one tip for advanced users.

items.question: How do I record and share what I made?
answer: The top bar has two keys. WAV records what you hear, so you can share it exactly as it sounds. MIDI saves the notes you played on the keyboards, so you can edit them later.

Tap once to start and once more to stop. After MIDI stops, the phone asks where to save the file. After WAV stops, a Recording finished window offers Master this take, which opens the Mastering window, or Save as-is, which asks where to save the plain WAV. While recording, a gold clock shows minutes and seconds.
MIDI does not include the drums, the loops, or the microphone. It holds only what you played on the keys.
To save one Looper or Mic channel as a WAV file, use Save on that channel. Export saves the whole project.
The Mastering window exports the finished song as WAV (24-bit), MP3 (320 kbps), FLAC (24-bit), or WAV 16-bit 44.1 kHz, and Share WAV + MP3 sends both. The files stay on your phone.

items.question: What are the Analog Mixer and the Mastering window?
answer: The Analog Mixer opens with a tap on LIVE SCOPE at the top of the screen. Drums, Looper, and Mic each have a strip with Drive, HPF, High, Mid, Low, Comp, Pan, Width, M, S, and a fader. The Master strip works on the whole mix. SPECTRUM and MIX MAP show where the channels sit and where they clash. There are 8 presets.

The Mastering window finishes a WAV recording or an imported song for streaming. Pick one of 8 styles, listen to A (before) and B (the style), then tap Start mastering and export. It opens after a WAV recording (Master this take) or from MASTERING in Settings.
Version 1.12 brings both, and it is on Google Play now.

items.question: Can I use my own sounds and audio files?
answer: Yes, on the Drum rows and on the Looper channels. Mic channels have no Load: they record from the microphone, and Save writes a WAV file.

Drums: on the Drum screen, a tap on a row name (Kick, Snare, and so on) opens a sound list. Load on the row picks one audio file, and LOAD on the LOADED tab picks one or several at once. Each of the 8 rows has its own LOADED bank of up to 88 samples, and the current rhythm plays the last file added. You can trim any sample in the list and shape it with GAIN, SQUEEZE, ATTACK, SUSTAIN, RELEASE, and REVERB, and the sample keeps those settings.
Looper: Load on a channel picks an audio file for that channel and replaces the take on it. Redo can't bring the old take back. There are 32 channels, one file each.

Which files: any audio file that your phone's Android can play and decode. L Studio has no format list of its own, so a format your phone can't decode fails with a message (Could not load audio, or Could not load the audio file).
How it is read: a stereo file is mixed down to mono. Any sample rate is converted to the app's rate, which is your phone's audio output rate (44.1 kHz if the phone doesn't report one).
Length: for a drum row, a file longer than 30 seconds keeps its first 30 seconds, and the app tells you. For a Looper channel, a file longer than 30:00 is cut at 30:00 with no message.
In LIVE mode Load is locked. Go back to PRO to load.
While a file loads into a Looper channel, a LOADING AUDIO window shows the real progress, and CANCEL stops it.
Mastering: Import audio file in the Mastering window opens a song from the phone (WAV, MP3, AAC, FLAC, or M4A). It is decoded on the phone and never uploaded.

items.question: What's the difference between a Preset and a Session?
answer: A Preset saves one sound, including which waves are on and, for each wave, its octave, its EQ, and its pages 2 to 4. It also keeps the Sound FX settings. A long-press on Presets quick-saves the current sound into the preset that is loaded.

A Session saves the whole project: the loops, the Mic channels, the drums, the presets, the Sound FX, the Loop page names and colors, the frequency presets, the drum sample picks, the LOADED drum samples your rhythms use, the Pad targets, the lyrics, and the Analog Mixer with its 8 presets. Mastering is per take and is not saved in the session.
New session empties the Looper and Mic channels. Kits, rhythms, and presets stay.

items.question: How do I back up my work or move to a new phone?
answer: Open the Load Console from Settings. Export all saves every session as one file, and Export selected saves only the highlighted session. Keep the file somewhere outside the app too.
On the new phone, use Import all or Import session and pick the file. An imported session whose name already exists gets a new name and does not replace the old one.
A Looper or Mic project alone has Export and Import on its own screen. Presets and drum styles have their own Save, Export, and Import in their windows.

items.question: What is the Load Console?
answer: In Settings, a tap on Load opens the Load Console. Each saved session is a row with a number and a name, and under the name are four keys: LOAD, SAVE, EDIT, and X.

LOAD loads the session. Before it loads, the app asks first and keeps an automatic backup of your current presets and drum kits. SAVE replaces the session with your current setup, after you confirm with Overwrite. EDIT renames it, and so does a long-press on the row. X deletes it, after a question.
Saving, loading, exporting, and importing show a progress bar with the real percent and a clear success or error message. You can't close it while the job runs.

items.question: Are there hidden actions worth knowing?
answer: Yes. Some actions have no button of their own, only a long-press or a hold.
Presets (Sound screen): a long-press quick-saves the current sound into the loaded preset.
A wave key on the Sound screen: a long-press opens its wave panel, with the octave, the EQ, and pages 1 to 4.
A rhythm number on the Drum screen (1 to 8): a long-press opens Pattern repeats, with COPY and PASTE.
Drum Kits (Drum screen): hold it to open Random genre, where you pick the genre that RANDOM uses.
A page number in the Looper: a long-press opens the page name and a color, from 8 colors.
A preset in Sound FX, Drum FX, Looper FX, or Mic FX: a long-press opens Amount, EQ, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset.
A session row in the Load Console: a long-press renames it.
A rhythm box in Loop Editor or Mic Editor: a long-press picks how many times that rhythm repeats, up to 88, and KEEP PLAYING.
1/4, 1/8, 1/16, and 1/32 on the Pad and on the Drum screen: hold to repeat at the drum BPM, release to stop. Hold STOP to fade out.
A preset number in the Analog Mixer: a long-press renames it. A double-tap on a fader sets it to 0 dB.
B in the Mastering window: hold it to compare with A. A saved My style: a long-press deletes it.
The number under a knob: a tap opens a box where you type an exact value.

items.question: How do I turn a few drum rhythms into a whole song?
answer: Long-press a rhythm number to open Pattern repeats and pick 1 to 10 repeats, type up to 88, or pick infinity or Default. Give rhythms 1, 2, and 3 the value 4, and the drums play rhythm 1 four times, then 2, then 3, and back to 1.
Rhythms left on Default are skipped. Infinity stays on that rhythm until you change it.

To copy a rhythm: long-press the rhythm you want to copy and tap COPY. Then long-press the rhythm you want to change and tap PASTE. The paste replaces its steps, samples, volumes, and sound knobs, and that rhythm keeps its own repeat count, BPM, and swing. REDO undoes a paste.

Looper channels can follow the rhythms too: turn on rhythm boxes in Loop Editor, and the channel plays only while the drums are on one of those rhythms. With KEEP PLAYING on, the take always plays to its end, even when the drums move on.

items.question: What are PRO and LIVE in the top bar?
answer: PRO is the normal mode, with everything open. LIVE locks some buttons so you can focus on playing, and a stray tap can't clear a take or load a file.

LIVE locks Clear on Looper and Mic channels, Load on the drum rows and on Looper channels, loading, renaming, and deleting LOADED drum samples, channel and page names, Import, and typing a number on a knob. In the Analog Mixer it locks renaming a preset.
It leaves open Rec, Play, Stop, mute and solo, Save, Export, switching pages, presets, switching drum kits, and everything you play. Another tap on the chip goes back to PRO.

items.question: I cleared or recorded over a take by mistake. Can I get it back?
answer: Yes. The Loop and Mic screens have a Redo key beside the page keys. It brings back the take you lost most recently on that screen: one you cleared, recorded over, or trimmed in the editor. It does not work while that channel is busy.
The Looper and the Mic each keep their own restore.
On the Drum screen, REDO in the header steps back one change per tap: steps, samples, volumes, left and right, sound knobs, and the rhythm, including CLEAR and paste.

items.question: How does Custom Frequency work? Can I tune my own scale?
answer: Yes. In Settings, the first row, Custom Frequency, opens Tune frequencies (Hz). Every key shows its frequency in Hz, and you can set it to the frequency you want. The keys start at 222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463, and 477 Hz.
If you want a starting point, there are templates: Major, Minor, Harmonic, Dorian, Mixolydian, Hijaz, Kurd, and Pentatonic, with D at 261 Hz. A tap on a name applies it.
My Presets has 8 buttons with names you choose. Save stores the current frequencies in them, and the frequency presets are also saved in a session.
The Key key on the Sound screen is something else: it only marks which keys belong to a scale. It does not change any frequency.

items.question: Can I save microtonal playing in MIDI? Can I connect a MIDI keyboard?
answer: Yes, but it is a recording saved to a file. The MIDI key saves a .mid file of the notes you played on the keyboards. Each note is saved as the nearest note plus a Pitch Bend that restores the offset from the exact frequency. The file assumes a Pitch Bend range of two semitones.
To hear the microtonal tuning, the program that opens the file must support Pitch Bend and be set to two semitones. Notes held together each get their own MIDI channel, so each keeps its own bend.
For now, L Studio does not support an external MIDI keyboard, and it has no live MIDI, neither input nor output. This is planned for later, with no date yet.

items.question: My mic recording is quiet, or it feeds back. What do I do?
answer: Quiet: raise Gain, which runs from 1x to 4x and starts at 2x. Then check the channel's Vol, from 0% to 100%. After a take exists, tap the channel's visualizer to open Mic Editor: in GAIN, 50 is the original level and 100 adds 12 dB.
Feedback: when Monitor is on, use headphones. Without headphones the phone warns about speaker feedback.
HPF cuts low rumble, from 40 Hz to 240 Hz. The first time you tap Rec, the phone asks for the microphone. If you said no, allow it in your phone's settings.

items.question: How many channels are there, and what are the limits?
answer: Looper: 32 channels, which is 8 pages with 4 channels on each. A recording can run up to 30 minutes, and at 30:00 it stops by itself.
Mic: six channels on two pages. A recording can run up to 4:00 on the three channels of the first page and up to 3:00 on the three channels of the second page. It stops by itself at the limit.

Drums: 8 rows (Kick, Snare, Hi-Hat, Perc, FX 1, FX 2, FX 3, and Voice), 8 rhythms in each kit, and 16 steps in each row. Each row also has a LOADED bank of up to 88 of your own samples, up to 30 seconds each, and a pattern repeat count goes up to 88.
Analog Mixer: three channel strips (Drums, Looper, Mic) and a Master strip, with 8 presets. Mastering: 8 styles and up to 12 saved My styles.

items.question: There is audio delay or crackling. What can I do?
answer: L Studio asks Android for low-latency audio on Android 8.0 and newer. On Android 7.0 and 7.1 it runs without that request, so the delay can be larger.
The delay also depends on the phone itself. In Settings, under Factory 64, Benchmark opens an audio test tool.
If the crackling or delay does not go away, write to support with your phone model, Android version, and app version.

items.question: How do I get help, and what about refunds?
answer: Write to dudichatam@gmail.com. It helps to include your phone model, Android version, app version, and what you did.
This website sells nothing and has no refund policy of its own. The purchase goes through Google Play, and for questions about a purchase you can write to the same address.
The Updates page on this site shows what changed in each version.

finalCta.title: Maybe it's time to find your sound.
finalCta.body: You can start from one sound, a beat, a loop, or a small idea. You never really know what will come out until you start playing.

guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: Pick a topic from the menu. Every topic ends with three tips for beginners and one tip for advanced users.

groups.title: Getting started

steps.text: A tap on MIDI starts a MIDI recording. Another tap stops and asks the phone where to save the file.
A tap on WAV records what you hear, after the Analog Mixer. Another tap stops, and the Recording finished window opens.
Master this take opens the Mastering window with that take. Save as-is asks the phone where to save the plain WAV file.

While MIDI or WAV records, a gold clock in minutes and seconds (MM:SS) shows between the title and the MIDI key. The minutes keep counting past 60. If both record, it counts from the one that started first.

PRO is the normal mode, with everything open. LIVE is a mode that locks some buttons, so you can focus on playing. It is good for recording and for performing, because a stray tap cannot clear a take, load a file, or rename a channel.
What LIVE locks: Clear on Looper and Mic channels. Load on the drum rows and on Looper channels. Mic channels have no Load key.
In the drum sound list, LOAD, RENAME, and DELETE. Import on the Loop and Mic screens, and Import in Drum styles.
Typing a number on a knob, while a drag still works. The names of Looper and Mic channels, the Looper page name, and the long-press that opens Page name.
In the Analog Mixer, LIVE locks the long-press that renames a preset.
What LIVE leaves open: Rec, Play, Stop, M, S, Redo, Save, and Export. The drum sample list and the sample arrows, CLEAR on the drums, switching pages, presets, and everything you play.
Switching drum kits stays open too: the DRUM KIT arrows, and Load in Drum styles, which loads the kit and closes the window.
Another tap on the chip goes back to PRO.

tipsBeginner: MIDI saves the notes you play, so you can edit them later. WAV saves the sound exactly as you hear it, so you can share it.
A knob's gold arc starts at the lower left, and 12 o'clock is the middle of its range. On L/R knobs the arc starts at 12 o'clock, the center.
On a phone the app stays upright, in portrait. On a tablet it can rotate.
groups.tipAdvanced: Some actions have no button of their own, only a long-press: a wave key (wave panel), a rhythm number (repeats), a Sound FX slot (tone), a Loop page number (name and color), Presets (quick save), Drum Kits (Random genre), a saved session (rename), and a mixer preset number (rename).

steps.text: L Studio has five screens: Sound, Pad, Drum, Loop, and Mic. The tabs under the scopes switch between them.
The top bar stays on every screen: the PRO or LIVE chip, MIDI, WAV, and Settings.
A tap on the scopes at the top (LIVE SCOPE) opens the Analog Mixer. On the Sound, Pad, and Drum screens a small Tap to open mixer tag shows where to tap.
A key marked (HOLD) does one more thing on a long-press, such as the wave keys and PRESETS on the Sound screen, and DRUM KITS on the Drum screen.

groups.title: Sound

sections.title: Wave panel: octave, EQ, and pages

steps.text: A long-press on a wave key opens the panel of that wave, under the wave row. The title shows the wave and the page, such as SQUARE 1 · EQ.
The keyboards stay open, so you keep playing and hear every change at once. Every change is saved by itself. CLOSE closes the panel.
A long-press on another wave key moves the panel to that wave. Leaving the Sound screen closes it.
The octave keys run from -2 to +2. A wave with its own octave shows it in a small badge on its key, such as -2.
That octave is fixed: -1 and +1 on the Sound screen move only the waves that follow the main octave. DEFAULT sets the page back to the main octave and a flat EQ.
The EQ knobs are LOW, MID, and HIGH, each from -12 to +12 dB, HPF from OFF to 2 kHz, LPF from 20 Hz to OFF, and GAIN from -24 to +6 dB. A drag turns a knob, and a tap on the value lets you type it.
The curve above the knobs shows the result. LPF at 0 Hz mutes that wave, and the curve reads MUTED BY LPF (0 Hz).
Every wave has 4 pages. Each page is one more voice of the same wave, with its own octave and EQ. Page 1 is always on, and a tap on the wave key turns it on or off.

Pages 2 to 4 have an ON and OFF key in the title row. The arrows beside the title, a swipe on the title or the curve, and the lamps under PAGES move between pages. A page that is off can still be edited.
A wave key with more than one page on shows the number of pages. A small dot means the wave has its own octave or EQ. Presets, the preset page file, and sessions keep all of it.
A tap on FX opens Sound FX. The keys still play while it is open.
There are 8 effects: Sub Forge, Depth Drop, Bass Clamp, Floor Pump, Iron Growl, Psy Orbit, Thick Vein, and Kick Bond.
A tap turns one on. A tap on the one that is on turns FX off. Only one is on at a time.
You can switch effects while you play. The change is smooth and the volume stays about the same. You hear the effect in the speakers, in a WAV recording, and in what the looper records.
The effects follow the drum beat. Before the drums have played, they run at 120 BPM.
After the drums stop, they keep the last drum tempo. Depth Drop drops again every 2 beats and on each new note.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that effect. Each of the 8 effects keeps its own settings when you switch. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 and changes all 8 effects, Sub Forge included.
The steps below are for version 1.13, which is in Google review and not available yet. Version 1.12 on Google Play works as described above.
In 1.13, Sound FX has 12 effects on pages. Step Ladder, Velvet Rotor, Mirror Tape and FM are new. Swipe left and right, or tap the arrows; the counter shows the page, for example 3/3.
With one keyboard and the settings closed, a page holds 8 effects. With two keyboards or the settings open, it holds 4. The window sits above the keyboards, so you keep playing.
FM is a real FM effect with 4 operators. Long-press FM for its knobs: RATE, ALGO, RATIO, INDEX, FEEDBK, DECAY and MIX.
Tap ALGO to choose one of 8 algorithms: A1 Stack, A2 Y, A3 Branch, A4 Twin mod, A5 2 Stacks, A6 1 to 3, A7 Stack+2 and A8 Organ. Each tile draws which operator modulates which.
RATE can be turned even while the drums play, and SYNC locks it to the drums again. On FM, FM | EQ switches the knobs between FM and EQ.
LOW, MID and HIGH work like the EQ of the waveform editor in every effect window: Sound FX, Looper FX, Mic FX and Drum FX. Each is plus or minus 12 dB in 0.5 dB steps, shown in dB.
A tap on Presets opens Presets, with 8 slots. Pages 1 to 8 are at the top. Under them are the page name and Edit page name, which changes it.

A long-press on Presets saves the current sound into the preset that is loaded, and the phone says Preset saved. If no preset is loaded, it says No preset loaded. When the window opens, it shows the page of the loaded preset.
A tap on Load opens the saved sound in that slot. A tap on Save stores the current sound there. A tap on Edit changes the name.
Save also stores the settings of all 8 Sound FX and which effect is on. Load brings them back exactly. Factory 64 presets and older presets load without changing the Sound FX.
Save also stores which waves are on, and Load lights them again. An older preset lights only its one wave. Save also stores the octave, the EQ, and the pages of each wave.

Under the page name, Import picks a page file and Save asks the phone where to store the page as a file. The page file also keeps which waves are on and the octave, the EQ, and the pages of each wave.
A tap on Key opens Scales. Pick Scale off, or a root from C to B under Major or Minor. A pick closes the window, and Key stays lit while a scale is on.
Custom Frequency is the first row in Settings. A tap opens Tune frequencies (Hz).
Each key shows its frequency in Hz. Set the keyboard to the frequencies you want, or play from a template.
Ready scales (D = 261 Hz) are the templates: Major, Minor, Harmonic, Dorian, Mixolydian, Hijaz, Kurd, and Pentatonic. A tap on a name applies that template, with D at 261 Hz.
Under the templates, My Presets has 8 buttons with your own names. A tap on one loads its frequencies into the keyboard and selects it.
Save stores the current frequencies in the selected preset, or in the first empty one when none is selected. Save* means there are changes that are not saved yet.
Reset is on the title row.
Default is above Close.

tipsBeginner: RIP brightens the sharp top edge. FUZZ adds dirty distortion. PHAZ adds a whooshy swirl. PIANO moves the tone toward a piano. Turn one on, play, and listen.

Attack is how fast a note starts. Release is how long it fades after you let go. Cutoff sets how bright the sound is, and Resonance adds a sharp color near the cutoff, so turn it only a little. Glide slides from note to note.

A scale only marks the keys that belong to it. It does not change the frequencies. Oct moves the whole keyboard up or down and keeps the relations between the keys. A wave with its own octave stays where you set it.
groups.tipAdvanced: Sound FX comes after WARM and after the P, G, and A keys, and before Drive. So Drive pushes the effect too. The speakers, the looper, and a WAV recording all hear the same result.

steps.text: Sine, Square, Triangle, Saw, and Noise sit under the scopes. A tap turns a wave on or off. Tap others to add or remove them, so several waves sound together.
One wave always stays on. Both keyboards play the lit waves. The screen starts on Saw.
Volume, Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release, Cutoff, Resonance, Echo Mix, and Glide are the knobs on the sound screen. A tap on the number opens a box where you type a value.
Drive is the slider on the sound screen. A drag sets the drive amount. A tap on Detune turns detune on or off.
A tap on RIP, FUZZ, PHAZ, or PIANO turns that one on or off.
A tap on -1 lowers the octave by one, down to -2. A tap on +1 raises the octave by one, up to 2. A wave with its own octave stays where you set it.
The keys read D, R, M, F, S, L, S, L. The number under a key is its Hz. They start at 222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463, and 477 Hz.
A tap on + opens a second keyboard above the first, one octave higher. The same + is on the Pad screen, and the second keyboard stays open when you switch between Sound and Pad.
The arrows beside PRESET load the next or previous saved preset. If none are saved, the phone says No saved presets.
The arrows beside DRUM KIT load the next or previous kit. They work in LIVE too.

groups.title: Pad
tipsBeginner: Hold a note first, then drag on the pad. The sound follows your finger while the note plays.
When you lift your finger, the pad glides back to the center, so the sound returns to normal by itself.
With the second keyboard open, the WAH, OCT, and Vibrato knobs hide to give the keys room. Close it to get them back.
groups.tipAdvanced: Turn on LOOP and DRUM as well as KEY. Holding a division then stutters the drums and your loops together, in time with the drum BPM, and holding STOP drops them out too.

steps.text: KEY, MIC, LOOP, and DRUM are the targets: they choose which sounds the pad moves. A tap turns a target on or off, and several can be on. KEY starts on.
The pad is marked L, R, HIGH, and BASS. Touch and drag to move the sound.
WAH, OCT, and Vibrato are knobs under the pad, from 0% to 100%. A drag sets them. They shape only the keyboard sound, not the drums, the loops, or the Mic.
A tap on SUB turns it on or off. The hint reads Bass -1 oct.
A tap on WARM turns it on or off. The hint reads Analog warm.
A tap on VIBE turns it on or off. The hint reads Soft vibrato.
P, G, and A sit in the voice row, on both Sound and Pad. P pumps the sound like a trance duck.
G chops it like a techno gate. A adds a slow frequency shift. You can turn on more than one.
Hold 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, or 1/32 to stutter the targets that are on, at the drum BPM. Release, and the stutter stops. Hold STOP to fade the targets out for as long as you hold it.

A tap on +, next to the voice row, opens a second keyboard above the first, one octave higher. The same + is on the Sound screen, and the second keyboard stays open when you switch between Pad and Sound. Another tap closes it.

groups.title: Drum

steps.text: The rows are Kick, Snare, Hi-Hat, Perc, FX 1, FX 2, FX 3, and Voice.

A tap on a row name opens a sound list for that row, from all the Factory kits, from the Exclusive kits when they are in the app, and for Voice also from Authentic. The LOADED tab holds your own samples for that row. Each row lists only its own kind of sound: FX 1 to FX 3 share one list, and Voice lists vocals only.
A tap on a sound puts it on the row and the list stays open. While the drums play you hear it on the next hit.

When they are stopped it plays once. The ◀ and ▶ arrows next to Load step to the previous or next sound. A tap on Load picks an audio file from the phone, adds it to the row's LOADED bank, and puts it on the current rhythm.
A drag on the row slider sets that row's volume. A drag on L/R moves the row between L and R.
SAMPLES sits next to DRUM KIT and shows the sample of the last row you used. Its arrows step that row to the previous or next sample.
The sound list of each row has a waveform of the current sample and six knobs under it: GAIN, SQUEEZE, ATTACK, SUSTAIN, RELEASE, and REVERB.
GAIN adds 0 to +18 dB. SQUEEZE runs from 0 to 100 and flattens the dynamics. ATTACK fades each hit in over 0 to 200 ms.

SUSTAIN sets how much of the sample is held, from 0% to 100%. RELEASE fades the sound out over 0 to 2000 ms, and the fade ends exactly where the kept part ends, also with SUSTAIN at 100%. REVERB sends 0% to 100% into the drum reverb.
Each row of each rhythm keeps its own sample and knobs, and they are saved with the rhythm into the kit.

LOADED is the last tab in each row's sound list, after FACTORY and EXCLUSIVE, and after AUTHENTIC on Voice. Each of the 8 rows has its own bank of up to 88 samples, saved by itself. The samples sit 10 to a page, with arrows to turn pages.
LOAD at the top of the LOADED tab picks one file or several at once, and shows how many samples the bank holds, out of 88. A file that is already in the bank is not added twice, it is selected.
A file longer than 30 seconds keeps its first 30 seconds. The last file added goes on the current rhythm.

The bar under the waveform sets where the sample starts and ends, and the part that is kept is shown in seconds. The original file never changes. Trim works on the samples in the list, also Factory, Exclusive, and Authentic.

SAVE keeps the trim and the six knobs with the sample, and every rhythm of the loaded kit that uses it on that row gets them. RESET puts back the full length and neutral knobs: SAVE keeps that, Close undoes it.
Close without SAVE goes back to what the sample had. Picking a sample brings its saved trim and knobs to the row.
RENAME and DELETE work on LOADED samples only. A name has up to 24 characters.
DELETE asks first, and every rhythm that used the sample goes back to the kit's own sample. LIVE locks LOAD, RENAME, and DELETE.
Sessions and the kit file you export from Drum styles carry the LOADED samples your rhythms use, with their names, trims, and knobs, so they open on another phone.
The arrows beside DRUM KIT load the next or previous kit. They work in LIVE too.
A tap on Drum Kits opens Drum styles. A long-press opens Random genre, and that is what HOLD says.
A tap on Rock, Trance, Rap, or Techno saves that genre and closes the window. Random on this screen uses that genre, and it starts as Rock. That window does not build a pattern by itself.
A tap on Switch to exclusive moves between the factory pages and the Exclusive pages.
There are 8 factory pages and 11 Exclusive pages. Each page has 8 kits.
A tap on a page number only shows that page. The kit loads when you tap Load.
A tap on Load loads that kit. A tap on Save stores the current kit under that name. A tap on Edit changes the kit name.
A tap on Edit page name changes the page name. A tap on Import picks a style file. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the page.
You can load a kit while the drums play. Sounds that still ring fade out in about 20 ms, so there are no clicks or distortion, and volume and pan glide to the new values in about 10 ms.
New hits use the new kit at once. A WAV recording hears the same clean change.
A tap on Drum FX opens Drum FX. A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off.
The presets are Street Boom, Vinyl Dust, Soft Chamber, Psy Drive, Techno Crush, Tribal Bloom, Goa Gate, and Wire Glitch.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.
A long-press on a pattern number opens Pattern repeats. The line under the title reads: How many times the pattern repeats before the next.
A tap on 1 through 10 sets that count.
For a higher count, type 1 to 88 in the field beside the infinity mark and confirm on the phone keyboard. A number above 88 becomes 88.
A tap on the infinity mark keeps it repeating. A tap on Default clears the repeat. Any pick closes the window.

RHYTHM, with COPY and PASTE, shows only when you open this window from the Drum screen. COPY copies the rhythm whose number you long-pressed. PASTE puts the copy into that rhythm and replaces its steps, samples, volumes, left and right, and sound knobs.
That rhythm keeps its own repeat count, BPM, and swing. REDO can undo a paste.
PASTE is off until you copy. COPY and PASTE close the window.

tipsBeginner: You can change steps while the pattern plays. You do not need to stop. Start the drums, then fix what feels off.
Your drum work saves itself: when you switch rhythm or kit, leave the Drum screen, send the app to the background, or save a session.
Random builds a pattern from the rules of the chosen genre. It is not pure noise. Pick a genre with a long-press on Drum Kits, tap RANDOM, and edit only what feels off.
groups.tipAdvanced: Chain rhythms into a song. Give rhythms 1, 2, and 3 a repeat count, such as 4. The drums play rhythm 1 four times, then 2, then 3, then back to 1. Rhythms left on Default are skipped when the drums move on, and infinity stays on a rhythm until you change it.

steps.text: A tap on PLAY starts the drums from the beginning. Another tap stops and returns to the start.
A tap on +4 shows FX 1, FX 2, FX 3, and Voice and hides the keyboard. The key then reads -4. Another tap hides those rows and brings the keyboard back.
A drag on Drum Vol sets the drum volume from 0% to 100%. A tap on the number lets you type a value.

A drag on Swing sets swing from 0% to 100%. A drag on BPM sets the tempo from 60 to 200. BPM, Swing, and the row volumes are live: a change you make while the drums play stays when the next pattern starts.
Hold 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, or 1/32 to repeat the drums at that division while you hold it. Release, and that repeat stops. Hold STOP to silence the drums for as long as you hold it.

A tap on a rhythm number, 1 through 8, loads that rhythm, including its tempo, swing, the sample on each row, the six sound knobs, the volumes, and left and right. Switching to another rhythm saves the one you leave into the current kit.
If the rhythm you switch to is empty, it starts as a full copy of the one you came from, and REDO can undo the copy. A long-press on a rhythm number opens Pattern repeats.
A tap on CLEAR, next to RANDOM, clears the steps of the current rhythm, sets its repeat count back to Default, and saves it. Its samples, volumes, and left and right stay.
REDO can bring back the steps and the count. A tap on RANDOM builds a new pattern in the chosen genre.
Each row has 16 steps. A tap turns a step on or off.
REDO, in the drum header, steps back through your drum changes: steps, samples, volumes, left and right, the sound knobs, and the rhythm. Each tap goes back one step.

groups.title: Loop

steps.text: A tap on a page number, 1 through 8, shows that page. A long-press opens Page name.
Type a name, pick one of 8 colors (orange, red, gold, brown, green, blue, purple, pink), and tap OK. Reset removes the color. Cancel keeps the old name and color.
The page color fills that page number and colors the channel waves on that page.
The name field next to Redo shows the name of the page you are on. A tap in it lets you type the name. Names and colors are saved with the loop project and in Export.
Each channel name starts as Ch and a number. A tap in the name changes it.
A tap on Rec starts recording. Another tap stops the take. If the channel already had a take, Redo can bring it back.
A take of the keys sounds exactly as you heard it live, with the echo and the octave and EQ of each wave.
A tap on Play plays the channel. Play stays off when the channel is empty, unless it is already playing or recording.
While the drums play, Play waits for the start of the next drum bar. Starting, stopping, and volume changes are smoothed.
A tap on Stop stops that channel for good. While the drums play, the rhythm boxes in Loop Editor do not start it again. It plays again only when you tap Play on that channel.
M mutes the channel and S solos it. M sits above the FX circle, and S sits above L/R. S turns gold while it is soloed, and every channel that is not soloed goes quiet, on all 8 pages.
You can solo several channels. A second tap on S takes the channel out of solo, and when none is soloed everything plays again. A channel that is both muted and soloed stays silent.
M is saved with the session. S is not saved, so a load starts with no solo.
The channel waveform keeps moving while the channel is muted or not soloed, so you still see the take. It shows the take before Vol, M, and S.
A tap on Redo brings back the take you lost most recently on this screen: one you cleared, recorded over, or trimmed in Loop Editor. It does not work while that channel is busy.
A drag on Vol sets the volume from 0% to 100%. A tap on the number lets you type a value. A drag on L/R moves the sound between L and R.
A tap on Load picks an audio file for the channel. While it loads, the LOADING AUDIO window shows the real progress, and CANCEL stops the load.

A tap on Save asks the phone where to store the channel as a wav file. Save stays off when the channel is empty. A tap on Clear clears the channel and its Loop Editor settings, and Redo brings back both.
A tap on Import picks a project file and loads the whole loop project. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the whole loop project.
A tap on a channel's waveform opens Loop Editor. It works when the channel has a take and is not recording.
A channel with saved edits gets a gold frame. You hear the changes while you edit.
Trim sets the part of the take to keep. Loop sets where the loop starts and ends.

Drum rhythms: 8 boxes, one for each drum rhythm. They choose which rhythm plays with the loop and how many times it repeats. A short press turns a box on, so the loop plays with that drum rhythm, or off again.

A long press opens Pattern repeats for that box: 1 to 10, a field where you type 1 to 88, infinity, or Default, which turns the box off. When the drums play, the channel follows the boxes that are on. With no boxes on, the channel keeps looping on its own.
KEEP PLAYING, at the bottom of that window, makes the box play the whole take. Each time the drums enter that rhythm, the take plays once from start to end, even if the drums move on or stop.

A count of 3 gives the first 3 entries one play each, and the count starts over when the drums play from the start or you switch kits. With infinity, the take plays again and again while the drums stay on that rhythm, then plays to its end.
Turning KEEP PLAYING on for a box that is off lights the box with a count of 1. Without it, a drum STOP fades the channel out gently instead of cutting it.
LOW, MID, and HIGH run from -30 dB to +30 dB. MID HZ moves the middle band from 100 Hz to 8 kHz. GAIN and SQUEEZE run from 0 to 100.
Reset sets everything back to the start values. Close leaves without saving.
Save keeps the changes, and a trim cuts the take. Redo can bring back the take from before the trim.
The editor settings are saved with the loop session and in the exported project.
Looper FX opens from FX on a loop channel.
A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off. The presets are Hook Glue, Spoken Soft, Indie Wash, Trance Stack, Phrase Throw, Double Lane, Pulse Gate, and Dust Weave.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.

tipsBeginner: A loop records your keyboard sound as it is at that moment, with your Sound FX. Changing waves, Drive, or Detune later does not change a take you already recorded.
While a channel records, your moves on the Pad are recorded with it. They replay with the loop. To change them live, turn on LOOP on the Pad and touch it.
In the editor, GAIN 50 is the original level. 0 is silent, and 100 adds 12 dB.
groups.tipAdvanced: With at least one rhythm box on, the channel plays only while the drums are on one of those rhythms, and stays silent on the others. A box set to 3 plays the loop 3 times when the drums enter that rhythm. Infinity keeps it going as long as the drums stay there. With KEEP PLAYING on, the take always plays to its end, even when the drums move on.

steps.text: There are 32 looper channels: 8 pages, 1 to 8, with 4 channels on each page. A recording can run up to 30 minutes. At 30:00 it stops by itself.

groups.title: Mic

steps.text: A tap on a channel's visualizer opens Mic Editor. It works when the channel has a take and is not recording.
It is the same editor as Loop Editor: Trim, Loop, the 8 drum-rhythm boxes, EQ, Gain and Squeeze. A long press on a box opens the same Pattern repeats, with the 1 to 88 field and KEEP PLAYING.
Save keeps the changes with the mic project. Redo can bring back a take from before a trim.
A tap on Mic FX opens Mic FX for that channel. Under the name it shows FX, and Off or the preset number.
A tap on a preset selects it. A tap on the selected preset turns it off. The presets are Street Punch, Phone Line, Talk Clarity, Neon Throw, Pulse Delay, Twin Voice, Garage Slap, and Wire Grit.

A long-press opens Amount, EQ Low, EQ Mid, EQ High, Mid-sweep, Transpose, and Reverb for that preset. Transpose runs from -12 to 12 semitones. Those sliders stay only while that preset stays selected.
A tap on Lyrics opens Lyrics. The window opens paused.
A tap on Edit lets you change the words. Done leaves editing. A tap on Play starts the scroll.
A tap on A- makes the text smaller. A tap on A+ makes it larger.
A drag on Speed sets the scroll from 20 to 150. It starts at 60.
The X and Close close the window and keep the words.

tipsBeginner: Mic has six channels on two pages. The keys 1 and 2 at the top switch pages.
The first time you tap Rec, the phone asks for the microphone. Allow it. Do a short test take before a long one. With Monitor on, use headphones, or the speaker feeds back into the mic.
HPF cuts low rumble. Gate turns the mic down when you are quiet. Pres raises or lowers the bright, high part of the voice.
groups.tipAdvanced: Transpose in Mic FX shifts the pitch of your voice without changing its length, from -12 to 12 semitones. At 0 the voice is left untouched.

steps.text: A tap on Redo brings back the take you lost most recently on this screen: one you cleared or recorded over. It does not work while that channel is busy. Mic and Loop keep separate restores.
A tap on Monitor turns the monitor on or off. If it is on and headphones are not connected, the phone warns about speaker feedback.
Gain, Mon, HPF, Gate, Low, Pres, and Comp sit under the heading. Gain runs from 1x to 4x.
HPF runs from 40 Hz to 240 Hz. A tap on the number lets you type a value.
Channel names start as Vocal 1, Vocal 2, Vocal 3, Guitar, Bass, and Inst 3. A tap in the name changes it.
A tap on Rec starts recording. Another tap stops.
A tap on Play plays the channel. Another tap stops. If the channel already had a take, Redo can bring it back.
A tap on Stop stops that channel for good, the same way as in the Looper. It plays again only when you tap Play on that channel.
S sits left of the FX circle, and M sits right of it, next to Vol. They work like M and S in the Looper.
Solo covers the Mic channels only: the Mic and the Looper each have their own solo. M is saved with the session. S is not.
The channel waveform keeps moving while the channel is muted or not soloed. It stops only when the channel itself stops.

A tap on Clear clears the channel and its Mic Editor settings, and Redo brings back both. A tap on Save asks the phone where to store the channel as a wav file. Save stays off when the channel is empty.
HPF and Pres on the channel affect only that channel. The channel has no Gate knob.
A drag on Vol sets that channel's volume. A drag on L/R moves the sound between L, the center, and R.
A tap on Import picks a project file and loads the whole mic project. A tap on Export asks the phone where to store the whole mic project.

groups.title: Analog Mixer

steps.text: SPECTRUM shows the sound of each channel by frequency: red for the drums, gold for the looper, and blue for the mic.
MIX MAP shows where the channels sit and marks where two of them clash, such as 100 HZ D+L. The view never changes the sound.
Presets 1 to 8 sit at the bottom. A tap on a number selects it, and a saved one loads. SAVE stores the mixer in the selected number.
A long-press on a number renames it, and the name shows next to the title. LIVE locks renaming.
DEFAULT sets the whole mixer back to its start values, with BUS off, and UNDO brings it back for a few seconds.
A WAV recording hears the mixer, and a session saves it with its 8 presets.

tipsBeginner: Start with the faders. Bring the loudest channel down before you turn anything else.
MIX MAP shows where two channels fight for the same frequencies. Cut a little with MID or LOW on one of them, and the other one opens up.
M mutes a strip and S solos it, so you can hear one channel alone while you set it.
groups.tipAdvanced: If BUS was on when you recorded a take, the Mastering window warns that the take would be compressed twice, and offers Master comp off or Keep both.

steps.text: A tap on the scopes at the top (LIVE SCOPE and DRUM SCOPE) opens ANALOG MIXER. CLOSE closes it and keeps its settings.
There are four strips: DRUMS, LOOPER, MIC, and MASTER. They stay in this order in every language.
Each channel strip starts with DRIVE, from 0 to 100%, and HPF: OFF, 50, 80, 160, or 300 Hz.
HIGH, MID, and LOW run from -15 to +15 dB, and HIGH works at 12 kHz. The chip under MID picks 360 Hz to 7.2 kHz, and the chip under LOW picks 35 to 220 Hz.
COMP runs from OFF to 10, and the chip under it picks 2:1, 4:1, or 10:1. PAN moves the channel left or right, and WIDTH runs from 0 to 150%.
Under the knobs are a GR meter, M and S, and a fader up to +10 dB. A double-tap on a fader sets it to 0 dB.
The MASTER strip works on the whole mix, keys included, before the final limiter. It has BUS, WIDTH, a BUS ON or OFF key with 2:1, 4:1, or 10:1, BAL, TRIM from -12 to +12 dB, and a fader up to +6 dB.
BUS starts OFF, and turning the BUS knob while it is off turns it on. LIMIT lights when the final limiter works. CLIP lights when the mix would clip without the limiter, and a tap on CLIP clears it.

groups.title: Mastering

steps.text: A plays your take before, and B plays it with the style. Hold B to compare. Match plays both at the same loudness, for listening only.
There are 8 styles: Clear Stage, Night Floor, Iron Loud, Rap Punch, Spoken Clear, Stream Peak, Sub Vault, and Glass Edge. Each has its own sound and loudness target in LUFS.
The style list marks the best match for your take. A tap on a style and on Play lets you hear it at once.
Intensity sets the style to Light, Normal, or Heavy.
Save as my style keeps your settings as My style, up to 12. A long-press on a My style deletes it, after a question.
Start mastering renders the full master. Save as-is (unmastered WAV) keeps the take without mastering.
While it works, a line shows the percent and the current step, and Cancel render stops it.
Advanced adds Undo and Redo for your changes. A tap on Reset sets Low, Mid, High, Output, Blend, and Width back, and a long-press on Reset resets everything.
The waveform shows After, Before, Comp, and Limit, and the magnifier zooms it.
Under it are the loudness in LUFS, the true peak in dBTP, LRA, and PLR, with Good or Check and a short hint.
The style chip and Light, Normal, and Heavy stay on top while you work in the four tabs below.
Tone: Low, Mid, and High for the whole song, from -6 to +6 dB, with the EQ curve before and after. Auto tone fixes the tone of the song before the style.
Reference track matches the tone, loudness, and width to a song you choose. Choose a song picks it from the phone, and Remove takes it away.
Dynamics: Comp on or off, Ceiling at -1 or -2 dBTP, Output from -12 to +6 dB, and Blend. Rap Punch, Iron Loud, and Sub Vault use 3-band compression.
Stereo: Width from 0 to 150% and the correlation meter. Mono and Phone check let you hear the song as on a phone speaker.
Loudness: the loudness over the whole song, before and after, and Target from -20 to -8 LUFS. A target louder than -14 LUFS uses a -2 dBTP ceiling.
A warning shows when a take hit the live limiter while it was recorded.
Export unlocks when the master is ready. Export WAV gives 24-bit, Export MP3 gives 320 kbps, and Export FLAC gives 24-bit. WAV 16-bit 44.1 kHz is for distributors.
Master saved shows the style, the intensity, the length, and each saved file.
The table shows before and after: integrated loudness, true peak, loudness range, PLR, and stereo correlation, next to the -14 LUFS streaming target.
Share WAV + MP3 shares both files. Export again and Master another take are there too.
The files stay on the phone, and nothing is uploaded. Closing the window brings the live sound back exactly as it was. Mastering is per take and is not saved in the session.
When you open the same take again, Continue mastering? offers your last settings.

tipsBeginner: Tap a style and press Play. You hear it at once. A is your take before, B is the style.
Keep Match on while you compare. It plays A and B at the same loudness, so you judge the sound and not the volume.
If a take is very quiet, record it louder. The window lifts a quiet take by up to 12 dB only.
groups.tipAdvanced: Hold B for a quick compare, and try Phone check before you export: many listeners first hear a song on a phone speaker.

steps.text: The Mastering window finishes a song for streaming. It opens after a WAV recording with Master this take, or from MASTERING in Settings.
Beginner and Advanced at the top switch the view. Close mastering asks first if the master is not exported yet.
You can master Last recording, or Import audio file, which opens a WAV, MP3, AAC, FLAC, or M4A file from the phone. The file is decoded on the phone and never uploaded.
Trim start, Trim end, and Full set the part to master. Zoom or a pinch zooms the waveform.

groups.title: Settings and sessions

steps.text: New session is the first row. It asks for a session name, then empties the Looper and Mic channels.
Kits, rhythms, and presets stay. If the name is already taken, it asks before it overwrites.
A tap on Save as opens Save Console. A saved session keeps the Sound FX, the loop page names and colors, the frequency presets, and the lyrics.
It keeps the drum sample picks, the Factory and Exclusive drum banks, the LOADED samples your rhythms use with their trims and knobs, and the saved settings of the other samples.
It keeps the octave, the EQ, and the pages of each wave, which waves are on, the two-keyboard view, and the pad targets.
It also keeps the Analog Mixer with its 8 presets. An older session loads with the mixer at its start values.

Saving, loading, exporting, and importing a session each open a window with a progress bar and the real percent. It stays at 99% until the work is truly finished, and it cannot be closed while the job runs. A second job is refused with the message Another session action is still running.
A tap on Load opens Load Console. Each saved session is a row with its number and its full name on one line. Under the name are four keys: LOAD, SAVE, EDIT, and X.
LOAD loads that session. Before a session loads, the app asks first and keeps an automatic backup of the current presets and drum kits. Mic monitor is off after a load.
SAVE replaces that session with the current setup, after you confirm with Overwrite. Cancel closes the question.
EDIT renames the session, and a long-press on the row does the same. If the new name is already taken, it asks before it overwrites.
X deletes the session, after it asks Delete session?
Export all saves every session as one file. Export selected saves only the highlighted session as one file. With Export all and Import all, the whole setup moves to another device.
Import all and Import session both read a file you exported. An imported session with the same name as one on the phone gets a new name instead of replacing it.
A tap on a row highlights it. The Load key at the bottom loads the highlighted session, and Cancel closes the window.

tipsBeginner: A Preset keeps one sound. A session keeps the whole project: the loops, the Mic channels, the drums, and the presets.
The tour has a menu of stations. You can skip, resume where you left off, or finish from the menu.
Export all makes one file with every session. Keep it as a backup, or use it to move to another phone with Import all.
groups.tipAdvanced: Restore Factory 64 overwrites any changes you made in the Factory presets and in the Style and Exclusive drum packs. Save a session first: it keeps your presets and drum banks, so you can load your version back.

steps.text: A tap on Language closes Settings and opens Choose language. Continue applies the language.
A tap on Show tutorial starts the tour again.
A tap on Factory 64 asks Restore Factory 64? Restore replaces the Factory 64 presets, all 8 Style drum packs, and all 11 Exclusive packs, then loads slot 1 on page 1. Cancel closes the question.
A tap on Benchmark, under Factory 64, opens the audio test tool.
A tap on MASTERING, the last row, opens the Mastering window with your last WAV recording, if there is one. The row is hidden while WAV records.

factory64.title: L Studio
factory64.subtitle: Eight Pages. Sixty-Four Voices.
intro: A complete sound library for L Studio: eight loadable pages, eight named presets on each page. Every voice is written to the app's native page format - volume, ADSR, cutoff, resonance, echo, glide, waveform, octave - on the instrument's home scale (222, 299, 333, 355, 396, 444, 463, 477 Hz).
Built for trance, techno, rap, trap, and metal. No generic "init" slots. Each page is a single musical job.
factory64.includes: 8 JSON pages · 64 named presets · ready to import from Preset
factory64.coverAlt: L Studio Factory Pack eight preset pages grid: Black Well, Gold Hammer, Light Knife, Gray Engine, Low Snake, Saw Teeth, Gold Fog, Spikes
factory64.oneLineList: BLACK WELL - subs · GOLD HAMMER - hits · LIGHT KNIFE - trance leads · GRAY ENGINE - techno · LOW SNAKE - 808 / trap · SAW TEETH - metal · GOLD FOG - pads · SPIKES - plucks
factory64.storeBlurb: L Studio Factory Pack - 8 pages, 64 voices. Black Well for sub and weight. Gold Hammer for hits. Light Knife for trance leads. Gray Engine for techno loops. Low Snake for 808 and slide. Saw Teeth for metal riffs. Gold Fog for pads. Spikes for plucks and stabs. Import one page at a time from Preset. Named, tuned, and voiced for the instrument - not converted from another synth. Plus: 8 Pro drum kits, including Experimental with 8 loaded channels.

pages.name: BLACK WELL
pages.body: Sine and triangle subs at octave -2 (key one sits at 55.5 Hz), plus saw basses with the filter shut. Long release, little echo, glide only where the note should crawl.

pages.name: GOLD HAMMER
pages.body: Synthetic percussion. Noise and square, attack at 5-6 ms, sustain near zero. Cutoff is the material: door at 700 Hz, hammer at 1400, wood at 1900, tin at 3400, whip at 4800, glass at 7800.

pages.name: LIGHT KNIFE
pages.body: Open saw and square leads. High cutoff, high sustain, echo as hall not wash. Octave +1 on the top voice. Rise and pull use slower attack and glide.

pages.name: GRAY ENGINE
pages.body: Stable oscillators for patterns. Cutoff stays in the 900-2800 Hz working band so the filter still moves. Resonance is the character, not decoration.

pages.name: LOW SNAKE
pages.tagline: Trap and rap. 808, slide, dark pluck.
pages.body: Sine 808s at 55.5 Hz. The tail is release, not decay. Slide is 160 ms glide. Concrete is the dry cut. Whisper is the quiet mix bass.

pages.name: SAW TEETH
pages.tagline: Metal and dark techno. Raw blade.
pages.body: Saw, square, and noise. Mid-low cutoff, resonance 0.36-0.58. Drive-oriented voicing. Low riffs at -1/-2, sparks at the top.

pages.name: GOLD FOG
pages.body: Slow attack (180-420 ms), long release (900-1800 ms), echo 0.20-0.38. Sine and triangle. Volume kept down because sine hits harder in this engine.

pages.name: SPIKES
pages.body: Attack 5-6 ms, sustain 0.06-0.16. Short notes that speak on the grid: trance bolt, techno step, trap ember, bell tail.

factory64.listenNote: Low frequencies are barely audible on phone speakers. For the full experience, use headphones or suitable speakers.
factory64.synthsIntro: Eight synth preset pages. Each page is one musical job, eight named voices.
factory64.launchNote: Available now on Google Play. L Studio Pro, $8.

factoryDrums.title: 8 drum kits.
factoryDrums.intro: 8 different kits, each with 8 drum styles. That is 64 styles in all, not 64 separate kits. From a rough acoustic sound to electronic rhythms and Experimental. Each kit brings a different character to L Studio Pro.
factoryDrums.closingBody: From acoustic Boom-Bap, through Indie, Techno, and Goa, to Experimental with 8 channels and built-in rhythms.
factoryDrums.closingLine: L Studio Pro lets you choose the sound that fits your direction and start creating.

kits.name: RAP 90'
kits.body: Acoustic Boom-Bap drums from the 1990s, with a warm, rough sound and an organic feel.

kits.name: HIP-HOP 2000s
kits.body: A mix of organic drums and 808, with an urban character and the energy of early-2000s hip-hop.

kits.name: SOFT INDIE
kits.body: Soft, intimate drums, brushes and delicate textures, with a kick that stays present.

kits.name: PSY PROGRESSIVE ROCK
kits.body: A mix of organic rhythms, percussion, and psychedelic energy, from the earth to space.

kits.name: BERLIN 90s TECHNO
kits.body: Dry, hard drums with an industrial character and a hypnotic groove inspired by 1990s techno.

kits.name: TRIBAL AMBIENT TRANCE
kits.body: Organic rhythms that build gradually, from mist and a first pulse, through a ritual and a peak, then a calm.

kits.name: GOA TRANCE
kits.body: Powerful electronic rhythms with a gradual build, from the first pulse to the energy peak.

kits.name: EXPERIMENTAL
kits.body: The most complex kit in the collection. 8 channels, including Kick, Snare, High, Perc, Bass, Texture, FX, and Vocal, with built-in rhythms and automatic transitions.

exclusive.title: Eleven packs.
exclusive.intro: A separate line from the eight Factory Drums kits. Eleven drum packs, each with 8 channels and 8 styles. Whoever buys Pro also gets the Exclusive pack free, at no extra cost, and there is no download button.
exclusive.homeTitle: Eleven special packs. Included with Pro.
exclusive.homeBody: Eleven Exclusive drum packs sit outside the Factory Drums set. Eight channels and eight styles in each pack. Whoever buys Pro also gets the Exclusive pack free, at no extra cost, and there is no download button.
exclusive.homeImageAlt: Fan of nine L Studio Exclusive drum pack posters
